data.narrative:
Physical Intelligence, a Series B AI & Software company, closed its last round at a $5.6B post-money valuation after raising $600M+. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of nine comparables—one public (Palantir) and eight private—spanning the same sector and adjacent development stages, including Figure AI ($39.0B, Series C), Scale AI ($29.0B, Series B), and Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A).

Two quantitative methods were applied. Stage-progression, using a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a forward valuation of $10.6B. Peer-median analysis across six same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $19.5B, with a range of $3.2B to $39.0B. The dispersion reflects heterogeneous risk profiles and progress within the frontier AI cohort.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $9.0B (low) to $22.4B (high), with a median of $15.1B. This implies meaningful appreciation from the $5.6B last post-money, though considerably below the peer median. Key uncertainties include the competitive intensity of the frontier AI market, near-term revenue trajectory, and the sustainability of current-stage funding multiples in this cohort. The wide peer range ($3.2B–$39.0B) underscores the difficulty in precise calibration at this stage.
